findings.reason: §9 makes "§5 goes first and is the only section that can start today", which collapses if §5 is already done; §5 must be re-scoped to its remaining half.
findings.text: §5's proposed repair is already landed: `_log_shows_the_command_ran` (commits a6fe28d74 "read a quoted command-not-found only absent a positive record" and 6e4d93d29 "require a positive record before trusting a quoted diagnostic") makes the guard at :1138 read the diagnostic only when no runner-summary or non-126/127 EXIT record shows the command ran — exactly §5's positive control; the plan's citation `promotion.py:464` and its claim "941fc6d4 added the guard and no repair commit exists anywhere in history" are both stale

findings.reason: a plan that re-derives a census instead of citing the existing one will build a parallel classification and a parallel test.
findings.text: §4 proposes a discharge taxonomy and a census test that "enumerates the refusal sites from the source"; reckon/crew/refusals.py already holds DISPATCH_REFUSAL_REMEDIES (D01–D23) with `format_refusal` appending "Resolve with …", and tests/test_crew_refusal_visibility.py:87 `test_every_reachable_family_calls_the_shared_formatter` already AST-walks REFUSAL_SOURCE_PATHS to assert every reachable family calls the shared formatter — the exact range-over-the-source assertion §4 says must be written before the change

findings.reason: §6 is described as a missing surface when it is a missing call site, and the design brief should say so.
findings.text: §6's done-when ("a refusal whose stated repair path is a repository file reports that file's live claim if one exists, naming the run, the node") is already delivered on the dispatch path: ScopeConflict (reckon/crew/node.py:431) constructs `run {run_id!r} (node {node_id!r})` and this test asserts `conflicting_run_id`/`conflicting_node_id` on the payload; the plan does not cite this test or the class, so the real gap (routing the promotion path through it) is understated

findings.reason: the deep change is a discharge column on the registry plus a formatter that emits it, not a second classification surface beside it.
findings.text: §4 classifies every refusal with one of three discharges "a property of the refusal rather than a judgement made at the call site", but promotion.py carries 80 `raise CrewError` sites and zero `format_refusal` calls, so implementing the rule at call sites spreads three-value classification across 80 raw raises instead of deepening the one registry that already maps every family id to its resolving action

findings.reason: without naming the owner, the implementer forks a second claim lookup that drifts from the one the dispatch path uses.
findings.text: §6 wants the promotion refusal to "name the claiming run, its node and its coordinator session"; ScopeConflict already builds the run/node half and format_refusal("D12") already appends its remedy, so a new claimant-resolution path in the promotion code would wrap machinery that exists — the plan must say why promotion cannot call the existing claim lookup that ScopeConflict and the dispatch path share

findings.reason: a forked refusal surface drifts from the owner, and this plan's own §2 already measures what happens when the discharge surface falls out of step with the refusal surface.
findings.text: §4's "asserted by a test that enumerates the refusal sites and fails on any that carries none" duplicates the owner of that exact mechanism: reckon/crew/refusals.py (registry) plus tests/test_crew_refusal_visibility.py:87 (the census that fails a family with no remedy); the plan should extend them with the discharge field rather than create a second refusal surface

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §4 spreads a new three-way discharge classification across the 80 `raise CrewError` sites in promotion.py rather than adding one column to the single existing refusal registry.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4 re-implements a refusal registry and a source-enumerating census that reckon/crew/refusals.py already owns.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan proposes machinery that already exists at reckon/crew/refusals.py (the D-code remedy registry and its census test) and does not cite it, and its §5/§6 prior-art account is stale against HEAD.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §6 reaches for a claimant surface the plan names only as "scope-conflict at dispatch" instead of the existing ScopeConflict class and its registered remedy.
